reason: VideoAgentTrek shows a new method working: inverse-dynamics labeling of unlabeled tutorial videos turned into pretraining data. It gives controlled gains over the same SFT stage (OSWorld-Verified 9.3 to 14-15.8%, AgentNetBench 64.1 to 69.3%), a data-scaling ablation and IDM accuracy evaluations, though there is no compute-matched control and the 50-step result is a single run. SWE-Bench Pro is a useful, harder resource, but as a paper it is thin on new ideas, with weak support for its contamination claims (GPL licensing is not a real barrier and the held-out set is unevaluated). Its numbers also contradict each other between the text and the tables (Sonnet 17.6 vs 16.3, GPT-4o 4.9 vs 3.9, failure-mode percentages), which hurts soundness.
